name: How much does design and architecture add to a whole-home renovation budget?

mainEntity.name: How much of my whole-home renovation budget should go toward design, architecture, and engineering?
mainEntity.text: How much of my whole-home renovation budget should go toward design, architecture, and engineering?

acceptedAnswer.text: For a simple refresh, design costs may be relatively modest. Once the project involves layout changes, structural modifications, or permit drawings, the design and engineering portion becomes more important. These services help prevent costly mistakes, align the contractor’s pricing with the real scope, and make permitting smoother. In complex Los Angeles projects, preconstruction services are often a critical investment because they reduce uncertainty before construction starts. Homeowners should ask whether fees are fixed, hourly, or percentage-based and confirm which deliverables are included. A well-developed plan often saves money later by limiting change orders and rework.
acceptedAnswer.description: Design, architecture, and engineering can take a meaningful share of a whole-home renovation budget, especially if the project includes layout changes or structural work. These costs are often best treated as part of the total project budget rather than an optional add-on.
